# R Markdown Demo

This is an R Markdown document. It's a file format that allows you to **write and** *format* **text**, while integrating your analysis results and plots.

You turn your R Markdown file into a polished document by clicking the `Knit` button. You can `knit` your `.rmd` file into a Word document, a PDF file, or an html file (which works great if you want to include interactive plots). 

R Markdown also works with citation managers. For example, I use Zotero as a reference manager. I can cite my references [@Henrich2010], and automatically generate a reference list at the end of the document.

## An example

Let's use the dataset `cars`, which comes pre-loaded in RStudio. This is what the data look like:

```{r cars}
head(cars)
```

I might want to include these data in a more manuscript-ready way (Table 1). We can also plot these data (Figure 1).

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

kable(head(cars), booktabs = TRUE, align = "l", escape = FALSE,
      caption = "This is the table caption.") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

```


```{r pressure, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Speed and distance were positively correlated.", fig.height=4, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

ggplot(data = cars,mapping = aes(x = speed, y = dist)) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth()+
  theme_classic()

```

\clearpage

## Reporting analyses

If I've run analyses, I will want to report the results of those analyses directly. For instance, let's report the correlation between `speed` and `dist` in the `cars` data.

Here is the code for running this correlation. I have also printed the results of the code.

```{r}

cor.test(cars$speed, cars$dist)

```

However, in a manuscript, we want to report these numbers in text. So I will first save the output of the test to an object (`cor_result`) and then directly pull the numbers I need from that object and print them in the text.

```{r include=FALSE}

cor_result_tidy <- cor.test(cars$speed, cars$dist) %>% broom::tidy()

# OR

cor_result <- cor.test(cars$speed, cars$dist) 

cor_result_tidy <- broom::tidy(cor_result)

```

Speed and distance were positively correlated (*r* = `r cor_result_tidy$estimate %>% round(.,2)`, *t*(`r cor_result_tidy$parameter`) = `r cor_result_tidy$statistic %>% round(.,2)`, *p* `r format.pval(cor_result_tidy$p.value, digits = 2, eps = 0.001)`).
